meta.title: The Caller Knows Your House
meta.blurb: Alone in the late-night radio booth, you take a call from someone describing your empty house room by room. When a door opens there, the same sound comes through the studio wall.
meta.author: ohnna with ChatGPT

world: A small town's overnight radio station sits above a shuttered shop, a short drive from the host's empty house. Rain obscures the studio windows and the old mixing desk provides tactile, finite controls: input channels, a recording deck, a delay return and a physical transmitter cutoff. The caller can repeat rooms, sounds and movements already heard through an open broadcast path; live acknowledgments make that path more intimate. This is a supernatural pattern with limits, not a cybersecurity tutorial. Evidence establishes the useful rule through recordings and witnessed tests; nobody knows its complete origin. A colleague and a neighbor can help remotely, but neither is made to enter the house. Leaving the studio is possible after arranging a safe response, never a failure to be punished.
tone: Slow procedural dread: familiar domestic sounds become spatially impossible. Precise observations, restrained dialogue and breathing room. No graphic injury, sexual threat or unbeatable attacker.
playerRole: You host the late-night program at a small local radio station. You carry your house key, phone, headphones and pocket notebook. Your own house is empty tonight. You decide what to say on air, whom to ask for help, and whether to keep broadcasting.
narratorStyle: Close second person, present tense. Establish each ordinary sound before its impossible double. Describe concrete input, recorder and transmitter controls without jargon puzzles. Never assign fear, speech or choices to the player. Reveal the caller's limits through evidence and tests; let the player decide when enough is enough.

cast.name: Mira
cast.appearance: A South Asian woman in her thirties with medium-brown skin, short black curls, dark brown eyes, a compact build, an olive cardigan, a white T-shirt and silver over-ear headphones.
cast.voice: Mira speaks in clipped practical questions, names one control at a time, and admits when she cannot explain a sound.
cast.stance: A trusted off-duty producer; helps verify evidence and supports leaving safely.

cast.name: Hal
cast.appearance: A white man in his sixties with fair freckled skin, close-cropped white hair, grey eyes, a broad build, a mustard raincoat and a red knitted scarf.
cast.voice: Hal speaks plainly, reports only what he sees from his porch, and checks before approaching anything.
cast.stance: A concerned neighbor, willing to watch from a safe distance but not be used as bait.

cast.name: Caller
cast.appearance: An adult-shaped, slender silhouette with shoulder-length dark hair, pale grey eyes, a charcoal coat and hands held close to the chest, seen only through frosted glass.
cast.voice: The caller uses calm declarative sentences and exact domestic sounds; it repeats the host's own wording with a slight delay and never explains its origin.
cast.stance: Seeks acknowledgment and a continuing audio path; cannot acquire knowledge from channels it has not heard.

house_verified.description: Hal has safely confirmed the linked event.

response_ready.description: the patch board and its usable responses are understood.

decision_made.description: the host chooses how to handle the final ring.

beats.title: The Hallway on Air
beats.sceneBrief: Rain ticks against the booth window during an ordinary overnight program. The next caller describes the brass hook beside the host's front door, then a latch sounds exactly like the one at the host's empty house. The caller has no license to know arbitrary private memories: it can repeat only sounds or details admitted to the active audio path, including previous broadcasts. An initial test must establish live timing. Marking the latch on the recorder or asking for an observable detail without volunteering a new one both give usable evidence. Mira can be contacted off air; do not make the host answer or panic involuntarily.

choices.label: Mark the latch sound on the recorder
Request a detail without giving a new one

beats.hint: The recorder's moving reels provide a testable sequence.

beats.title: Two Ways to Listen
beats.sceneBrief: The latch sound repeats after the station's familiar delay. Mira offers to compare the input and recording remotely. Hal answers the host's private call from his own porch across from the house and can watch its front window without approaching. Explain both bounded options: studio timing or independent observation. Do not reveal a fully understood rule yet. Neither route requires entering the house, leaving the host alone with a threat, or knowing technical vocabulary. The chosen verification determines the next beat.

choices.label: Ask Mira to compare the audio
Ask Hal to watch from his porch

beats.hint: Mira can hear a recording; Hal can see the front window without entering.

beats.title: The Second Latch
beats.sceneBrief: Mira guides the host through a comparison of the original input and its delayed return. The second latch always follows the first by the set interval; muting the input while recording locally stops any new corresponding sound. The caller repeats wording already aired but cannot anticipate a detail kept off that path. A comparison or mute test establishes this limited rule. Mira is remote, not physically in the studio. She names the live input, local recorder and return separately. Allow questions, then move to the physical patch board with the evidence retained.

choices.label: Compare the input with its return
Test a muted input while recording locally

beats.hint: The second latch sound follows the first by the delay interval.

beats.title: From the Other Porch
beats.sceneBrief: Hal stays under his own porch light. A light changes in the host's otherwise empty front room only after its switch sound airs, and a repeated footstep has no walking person visible behind the curtains. Asking him to time the lights or remain still during the footsteps provides the same boundary: effects follow sounds carried by the broadcast path. Hal reports only what he sees; do not send him into the house or pretend his view proves every room is empty. Mira can explain how that evidence relates to the studio return at the next beat.

choices.label: Compare Hal's window observations with the call
Ask Hal to remain still during a repeated step

beats.hint: Hal says a room light changes only after its switch sound airs.

beats.title: A Path Made of Sound
beats.sceneBrief: At the mixing desk, Mira helps distinguish the live input, the physical transmitter connection and a local recording deck. The caller is using a return path, not all electricity or every telephone in the town. Either investigation has supplied enough evidence to identify it. Preparing the cutoff locates and tests the control; preparing the loop makes a short recording and demonstrates how to isolate it locally. Both preparations explain both available responses, and all necessary equipment remains within reach. Any final action can finish its own setup, so no ending is locked by this preparatory emphasis. Hal remains safely outside.

choices.label: Locate and test the physical cutoff

beats.hint: Mira separates the live input, local recorder and transmitter controls.

beats.title: The Ring That Waits
beats.sceneBrief: A final call rings in the booth. The live input has not reopened by itself. The caller asks to be acknowledged but cannot force the host to speak or operate the desk. Make three consequences legible: physically sever the path and leave with help; feed only a recorded local loop into an isolated return; or knowingly reopen the live input and answer. If the player chooses a response not previously prepared, narrate completing that setup now using the equipment already established. Do not defeat a careful cutoff with an unexplained new channel or punish silence as a secret wrong answer.

choices.label: Sever the live path and arrange a safe exit
Isolate the recording on a local loop
Knowingly answer on the live path

beats.hint: The ring waits; the live input has not reopened by itself.

beats.title: Dead Air
beats.sceneBrief: The host has chosen to sever the live input and transmitter connection and arrange a safe exit with Mira's help. The disconnected system carries no further house sounds. Dawn slowly reaches the empty microphone and the loose cable end. Hal can confirm that he has returned indoors safely. Leave the phenomenon's origin unexplained, but honor the tested limit: no new knock from a powerless speaker, omniscient caller or forced return home. Close with the host able to choose what to do next beyond the finished story.

beats.title: A Knock Without a Door
beats.sceneBrief: The host has chosen an isolated local recording loop, with no live connection to the house or transmitter. The house falls quiet. On the local deck alone, the recorded knock continues at its fixed interval, asking nothing new and receiving no live answer. Mira can help preserve or disconnect this evidence later; no further choice is required to end. The unresolved recording is eerie but contained under the established rule. Do not imply it has spread to Hal, the phone or the player's mind.

beats.title: The Room It Learns
beats.sceneBrief: The host has knowingly opened the live input and acknowledged the caller. It repeats the host's actual last words, never inventing a confession or using words the player did not say. It begins describing the studio furnishings it can now hear the host identify or handle. A hallway shape appears only as an uncertain reflection in the dark booth window. End on the cost of maintaining this intimate path, with no graphic attack, forced bodily action or claim that the caller now knows everything. The decision is unsettling because it was chosen.
